review_method: Independent line-by-line read of all six cores plus advance/*, review_dispatch.py, escalation_ladder task generators, factoryd.py at the pinned SHA in a detached read-only worktree; execution paths traced by following call sites, not by running engines. No product writes during the review pass; every cited line re-verified against the pinned SHA.

findings.evidence: Lines 197-202 document the incident: the gate is bound to the exact integration SHA, so a repair landing at HEAD afterwards left the milestone re-validating the old red SHA every poll - 3 refusals, quarantine, a human. _rebind_gate_to_head_if_satisfied is called here as the in-house patch, but it only reopens missions when _prevalidated_product_head succeeds, and it adds its own memo defect (see the settlement.py:230 finding). The verdict reuse problem - the same validator/contract/SHA identity being proven twice - is still solved by ad-hoc state fields instead of one receipt-bound verdict store.
findings.fix: Challenger: bind validation verdicts to (contract, integration SHA, control pin) as durable receipts consumed once by settlement and rebind alike; no per-fix memo patches. No repair in this closed-list mission.

findings.evidence: memo[ctx.mid] = head is persisted at line 230 BEFORE _prevalidated_product_head runs at line 233, and nothing removes it when the probe fails or raises. Scenario: HEAD satisfies the contract but the probe's IndependentValidator crashes on a transient condition (locked refs, tmp worktree failure); this HEAD is now memoized forever, every later cycle returns None at line 228-229, the milestone falls back to MILESTONE_GATE_BLOCKED on the old bound SHA - the exact 22/09 replay loop re-enters through the patch that was meant to close it.
findings.fix: Challenger: write the memo only after a completed probe outcome and key it by full gate identity (contract+SHA+control pin), or persist the probe verdict itself and reuse it.

findings.evidence: probe_gate_first memoizes (contract_id -> head) at line 130 BEFORE run_clear_gate at line 131. Scenario: the probe is rejected once (QUARANTINE_GATE_PROBE_REJECTED, line 134) or the process dies right after the memo is saved; every later poll at the same HEAD hits line 128-129 and returns None with no event, no durable rejection proof and no counter - the supervisor silently answers 'nothing to judge' forever at that HEAD. The owner sees a quarantine that never exits and no evidence of why.
findings.fix: Challenger: make the probe outcome a durable receipt (contract+HEAD+gate inputs -> verdict) that later polls read instead of a bare 'already probed' memo; a missing or unprovable receipt must be retryable.

findings.evidence: The memo identity is only (contract_id, HEAD). Scenario: the first probe is red because a non-git prerequisite is transiently absent (engine CLI quota, a service the validation command calls); the prerequisite turns green later WITHOUT a product commit, HEAD does not move, so line 128 returns None before run_clear_gate on every poll - the 4 manual quarantine lifts of 22/09. Expiry or hand-editing state remains the only exit because the probe key cannot observe non-git inputs changing.
findings.fix: Challenger: key quarantine exit on the full gate identity including non-git inputs (env, quota snapshot, control SHA), and re-evaluate when any identity component changes.

findings.evidence: _acquire_worktree: when the worktree's base differs from the new base and the worktree carries its own commits, the only outcomes are rebase (clean tree, line 555-558) or archive (line 559) - nothing consults an already-green candidate receipt before archiving. Scenario: mission's candidate passed its judge but the milestone has not settled yet (multi-AI review pending); golden HEAD advances via another milestone; the rebase hits a conflict (or the tree is dirty after a crashed capture); the validated candidate branch is archived and fresh() restarts the whole build from HEAD, re-paying the model budget for work already proven green.
findings.fix: Challenger: a candidate registry owns green candidate identity across engine rotation; a validated candidate is adopted or explicitly superseded before any archive path.

findings.evidence: The min_distinct_accept<=1 branch dispatches via _review_dispatch.dispatch_review (line 515) with no engine_hint and no engine_quota_refused call - that guard exists only in the roster branch at line 557. Scenario: every contract frozen before CODEX-LOT-C37 (the branch comment says 'byte for byte unchanged') routes its single review through model_router's table; the table picks GLM while its quota observer is at refusal threshold; the launch burns the final quota window and the next cycle re-dispatches the same review - the 22/09 GLM-at-100% incident.
findings.fix: Delete the legacy branch: one quota-guarded roster path for one or N reviewers. Implemented by REVIEW_SINGLE_PATH_QUOTA_GUARD in this mission's closed list.

findings.evidence: _ss1_adopt_or_skip_pass tests state==MILESTONE_PARKED and parked_until>now at lines 37-39 and returns _CONTINUE at line 40 - before _ss2 ever runs. The only code that recognizes an OWNER allocation is the BASIS_OWNER branch (_ss2 lines 145-162 for a stranded cnp_ DIAGNOSE, _cnp_peek runtime.py:2511-2522 otherwise), both strictly later. Scenario: three equal fingerprints park the mission 6 h (park written at mission_dispatch.py:886-892); the owner issues a valid OWNER_AUTHORIZATION one minute later; every cycle skips at line 40 until wall-clock expiry - the 7th loop of 22/09, whose only exits are expiry or forbidden hand-editing.
findings.fix: Challenger: owner authorization is an event that cancels the park timer before mission selection - consult recovery_allocation.available() in the park test itself.

findings.evidence: except Exception: pass ('never block recovery on the cell') around persist_audit_cell_request for trigger REPEATED_EQUIVALENT_FAILURE. Scenario: disk full or a corrupt audit-cell dir makes the persist raise; the escalation ladder still advances (stage DIAGNOSE/REPLAN) so nothing looks stuck, but the multi-AI cell the CTO directive requires at the 3rd equivalent failure was never informed and no event records the loss - the audit obligation is silently skipped and the logs look healthy.
findings.fix: Emit a typed AUDIT_CELL_REQUEST_LOST event (same dedup discipline as LAUNCH_BLOCKED) when the persist fails; blocking recovery is not required, invisibility is the defect.

findings.evidence: The strict-hint quota parking block (lines 866-892) ends in except Exception: pass. Scenario: QUOTA_CUT on a phase-5 strict-hint mission; the quota snapshot is unreadable (JSON corrupt, HOME moved) so _qls raises inside the try; the exception is swallowed, MILESTONE_PARKED is never written and no MISSION_PARKED_FOR_QUOTA event exists; the next cycle re-dispatches the same engine at a refused quota - each poll burns a refused launch and the mission never parks, invisible to the owner.
findings.fix: Narrow the except to the snapshot read and emit a typed PARK_COMPUTATION_FAILED event; a park that cannot be computed must be visible, not skipped.

findings.evidence: "_pr" in dir() and getattr(locals().get("_pr"), "promoted_sha", ""): the split rewrite turned _pr into ctx._pr (assigned at line 699), so '_pr' is neither a local name in dir() nor in locals(); the condition is always False. Scenario: a golden promotion whose merge commit differs from the integration SHA; record_settlement_verified receives candidate_for_ledger = integration_sha (fallback lines 767-768) instead of the promoted_sha the branch was written to prefer - the settlement ledger names a commit that is not golden, permanently, with no error anywhere.
findings.fix: Read ctx._pr directly; delete the dir()/locals() relics of the rewrite script.

findings.evidence: Two unconditional 'return None' statements (lines 905 and 907) follow the final 'return rt.CycleResult("MILESTONE_SETTLED", ...)' at line 902 in _settle_promote_and_project. They can never execute; a reviewer tracing fall-through outcomes is misled into believing the function has a silent-success path.
findings.fix: Delete both unreachable returns - part of the real LOC reduction.

findings.evidence: proven_completed_milestones calls verify_settlement(..., run_acceptance=True) for every COMPLETE milestone, and verify_settlement re-runs IndependentValidator.validate at the exact same (contract, integration_sha, control_pin) that settlement already validated minutes earlier - with no memoization by validation identity. Scenario: base_ready_aggregator or settlement_blockers over a project with 5 settled milestones re-executes 5 full product_e2e suites (each up to 1800 s) on every readiness read; three call sites in one morning re-pay the same acceptance repeatedly and a 30-minute validator triples the wall clock of a status command.
findings.fix: Cache the acceptance verdict keyed by (contract_id, integration_sha, control_pin) with the receipt-bound verdict as the single source; re-run only when an identity component changes.

findings.evidence: The generated DIAGNOSE task file instructs the engine: 'Write evidence/recovery/{id}_diagnosis.json containing...' - but the real pipeline (dispatcher_v3.py:1418-1428) parses the engine's stdout JSON and the DISPATCHER writes the artifact itself; the dispatcher docstring even calls the launch read-only. Scenario: a docile engine spends its bounded turns creating a file in the worktree that no code ever reads (the acceptance test_cmd checks the dispatcher-written copy under project_dir), and a strictly read-only engine may report failure for being unable to comply with the write instruction at all.
findings.fix: Make the task file say what the pipeline actually does: emit the diagnosis JSON on stdout; delete the write-a-file instruction.

findings.evidence: _pump_to_sink + _run + the module-global _STREAM_SINK implement process groups (setsid), threaded stdout/stderr draining, redaction, group SIGKILL on timeout/exit and a raw NDJSON stream sink - and telemetry/adapters.py (1220 lines) then re-parses each provider's output format. Scenario: every new provider CLI needs another hand-built adapter plus its own kill/drain edge cases; a silent child holding a pipe open is a defect class this file keeps re-fixing (comment at line 190). harness.lol already normalizes supported agent CLIs to bounded NDJSON event streams and owns process-group lifecycle.
findings.fix: replaceable_by: {project: harness.lol, url: https://www.harness.lol/docs/reference/architecture, what_it_replaces: engine process-group lifecycle + stream normalization in dispatcher_v3 (_run/_pump_to_sink/_STREAM_SINK) and the per-provider parse adapters in telemetry/adapters.py, loc_removed_estimate: 1100, effort_days: 5, risk: medium}; Factory keeps its receipts, budget ledger and verdict taxonomy outside the adapter.

findings.evidence: _acquire_worktree is an in-house orchestration policy for parallel worktrees: base-drift detection, dirty-tree preservation, rebase-or-archive, fresh-at-HEAD - and it is exactly where the green-candidate-discard loop lives (line 552-559) because the policy has no candidate registry. Scenario: engine rotation makes every control-repo commit a stale base; the policy archives a branch carrying validated work because its only recovery primitive is the archive ref. Omnigent already assigns parallel tasks to isolated worktrees and routes the resulting diffs to a different-vendor reviewer.
findings.fix: replaceable_by: {project: Omnigent, url: https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent, what_it_replaces: fan-out worktree policy (acquire/rebase/archive) in dispatcher_v3 while keeping WorktreeManager as the thin git wrapper, loc_removed_estimate: 120, effort_days: 8, risk: high}; Factory keeps writer fencing and exact-SHA settlement.

findings.evidence: run_daemon_loop plus its four separate crash-reconciliation mechanisms (_load_or_create_state line 194, run_windows.open_run line 908, adopt_quarantine line 932, _harvest_parallel/_ADVANCE_FUTURES lines 415-526) own durable polling, restart recovery, quarantine adoption, retry cadence and worker harvesting in one 1300-line local daemon. Scenario: a crash between a state mutation and the next poll requires bespoke cross-ledger reconciliation spread over four mechanisms and two files; each new in-flight artifact (leases, streams, checkpoints) adds another reconciliation seam - this is precisely what a durable workflow engine persists and replays.
findings.fix: replaceable_by: {project: Temporal (sdk-python), url: https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python, what_it_replaces: daemon polling/restart/recovery/harvest ownership (run_daemon_loop + the four reconciliation mechanisms, ~900 lines), loc_removed_estimate: 900, effort_days: 12, risk: high}; Factory's authority gate, settlement truth and routing policy stay as activities.

findings.evidence: _create_detached_worktree/_remove_detached_worktree rebuild a throwaway clean room (mkdtemp + git worktree add --detach + SHA verify + teardown in finally, lines 154-189) on EVERY validation, twice over when a control pin is set (dual worktrees, lines 240-307) - host caches, python env and repo state can still differ between runs at the same SHA. Scenario: a validator green at home and red on the same SHA after an interpreter upgrade; nothing in the contract pins the environment, only the code. Harbor supplies versioned task definitions, container environments and test scripts for repeatable evaluation runs.
findings.fix: replaceable_by: {project: Harbor, url: https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor, what_it_replaces: validation environment assembly (detached worktrees + control pin execution) in IndependentValidator, loc_removed_estimate: 140, effort_days: 5, risk: medium}; Factory keeps the exact-SHA authority decision and the verdict taxonomy - only the execution environment moves.

findings.evidence: _cnp_peek is a fourth partial owner of 'resume/retry' semantics - it grants, parks (3-fingerprint park at 2529-2555), creates DIAGNOSE work and consumes standing authorizations - alongside _ss2's escalation ladder (mission_dispatch.py:130-296), quarantine_ladder's repair chain, and _cnp_regrant_stranded_diagnose (runtime.py:2426) whose sole purpose is closing a crash window BETWEEN two of the other owners. Scenario: an owner allocation is honored by _cnp_peek's branch but can never be reached because mission_dispatch applies its own park policy first (the 7th 22/09 loop); each owner fixed its own crash seam (comment at 2428: 're-grant the EXACT stranded DIAGNOSE, once') instead of one owner holding resume responsibility.
findings.fix: Challenger: one workflow owner for restart/retry/resume (the Temporal ADAPT decision); the CNP peek, the ladder and the regrant closer collapse into activities it schedules.

files_reviewed_clean_notes.factory/lib/worktree_manager.py: Read in full (387 lines): a thin, careful git-worktree wrapper - CAS update-ref fast-forward (103-109), CAS branch quarantine preserving commits (119-135), inherited-meta noise filtering in recover_worktree (263-271), refresh/rebase/archive with explicit invariants. No loop, dead code or duplication found here; the replaceable ORCHESTRATION policy around it lives in dispatcher_v3._acquire_worktree (see finding at dispatcher_v3.py:518). Class: keep.

refutations.DIAGNOSE_WITHOUT_WRITE_SCOPE: Refuted at the reviewed SHA by tracing the diagnose execution path end to end: runtime._execute_recovery_work builds an autopilot exec_dict whose test_cmd only validates the artifact JSON (runtime.py:680-701); dispatcher_v3's diagnose branch launches the engine, parses its STDOUT (recovery_agent_message + extract_json_object, dispatcher_v3.py:1418-1426) and the DISPATCHER itself writes evidence/recovery/<id>_diagnosis.json (dispatcher_v3.py:1427-1428) under --project-dir. The engine never needs write access, so 'diagnose launched without the right to write anything' is not explained by a missing write edge in this code. The historical 4xCodex incident is more plausibly a stdout-parse failure (DIAGNOSIS_EMPTY at 1411-1417) or the stale task-file instruction that still asks the engine to write the file (escalation_ladder.py:989, filed as DUPLICATE).
